desc: Ideation: identified group-merging, per-step sign-vector structure (+...+,0?,−...−), derived algebraic conditions (Δ nonincreasing, y_j parity/plateau constraints); found counterexample to naive "match k-th 1 to k-th 1" plan (samples 1 and 3 require merges; sample 3 needs plateau-aware assignment)
Brute-force BFS for tiny N; harness comparing BFS vs min-over-surjections model with plateau-parity condition implemented

Run the harness on all n ≤ 6 cases; inspect mismatches to validate/refute the plateau-parity characterization and the min-over-surjections formula — 3969 cases, 0 mismatches; characterization validated

Design an efficient algorithm (sum N ≤ 1e6): greedy min-max assignment + plateau-parity check + local repair for mixed parities (options: bump last group of plateau up when c<0, force first group down + re-greedy when c>0)

Stress-test the efficient solver against the brute-force BFS/model on random small cases (n ≤ 8, many random A/B) to confirm the greedy + repair logic, especially mixed-parity repair paths — all three phases pass with 0 mismatches after fixing repair propagation, s=0 guard, and tie-break handling
Verify the fixed solver on the three provided samples (expect 3, -1, 5) and confirm edge cases (m = r bijection, single group, single target, plateau-parity infeasible → -1)

Analyze worst-case complexity of the repair loop (number of plateau runs × O(m) re-greedy); if pathological O(m²) is possible, memoize or restrict repairs to the cheapest run per parity class; verify performance on N = 1e6
Write final production main() with fast I/O and do a final end-to-end run
